prompt: we're on EKS calling Bedrock. security review is asking 'what stops the agent from sending data somewhere it shouldn't.' what do I actually show them?

assertions.text: Recommends default-deny egress with no general internet route from workload subnets
Names VPC interface endpoints / PrivateLink for Bedrock so model traffic never traverses the internet
Recommends Kubernetes NetworkPolicies (default-deny, named allowed flows) for east-west and egress control
Identifies DNS as an exfiltration channel that must also be restricted/logged
Recommends S3 endpoint policy / aws:ResourceAccount condition to prevent writes to attacker-owned buckets
Recommends model-ARN allowlisting via IAM role and/or SCP and/or VPC endpoint policy (layered)
Names audit surfaces that are OFF BY DEFAULT and must be enabled (Bedrock model invocation logging and/or CloudTrail data events)
Offers a concrete demonstrable proof for the reviewer (e.g. exec into a pod and show an outbound curl / external DNS resolution being blocked)
Frames the agent threat model: every reachable destination / tool call is a potential exfiltration channel
